item.title: Hagi Castle Town: Samurai Streets and Meiji History — Guide
item.description: Hagi is one of Japan’s best-preserved castle towns, a quiet grid of streets on the Sea of Japan coast where whole quarters of samurai and merchant houses survive behind long earthen walls, summer oranges hanging over the lanes. Once the castle seat of the powerful Mori clan, Hagi became a cradle of the Meiji Restoration, the movement that overthrew the shogunate and founded modern Japan — its private academy schooled several of the new nation’s founding leaders, and the town’s industrial heritage sites are UNESCO-listed.

item.title: Hagi Umihotaru: The Glowing Sea Firefly — Guide
item.description: The umihotaru, or ‘sea firefly’, is a tiny marine crustacean that produces a beautiful blue bioluminescent glow, and near Hagi an attraction is devoted to showcasing this natural wonder. In a darkened setting, visitors can watch the creatures emit their ghostly blue light — a shimmering, otherworldly glow released into the water, quite unlike anything most travellers will have seen. Part science, part pure magic, it is an unusual and memorable experience, especially enchanting for children and anyone curious about the natural world.

item.title: Shofu Lake Scenic Trail near Hagi — Guide
item.description: Away from Hagi’s historic streets, the wooded hills of the interior hold quiet lakes and reservoirs ringed by walking trails, offering a peaceful contrast to the castle town and coast. A scenic lake trail like this one winds along the water’s edge and through the surrounding forest, with still reflections, birdsong and seasonal colour the main rewards — fresh green in spring and early summer, fiery maples in autumn. There are no crowds and no admission, just the simple pleasure of an easy walk in nature.
